name: Mauritius

facts.religion: Hindu about 48%, Christian about 32%, Muslim about 17%

snapshot: A small island democracy that grew rich through sugar, textiles, tourism and finance, and recently secured sovereignty over the Chagos Islands from Britain.
culture: Mauritius had no native population; its people descend from Indian indentured labourers, enslaved Africans and Malagasy, French settlers and Chinese traders. Mauritian Creole is the shared language, with English and French also used. Hindu festivals like Maha Shivaratri, when hundreds of thousands walk to the sacred lake Ganga Talao, share the calendar with Christian, Muslim and Chinese holidays. Sega music has roots in slavery.
society: Mauritius is one of Africa's richest countries per head, with a welfare state, free education and healthcare. Its economy moved from sugar to textiles, tourism and offshore finance. Politics has long been dominated by a few families. A 2025 treaty transferred the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, with Britain and the US keeping the Diego Garcia base on a 99-year lease.
situation: Navin Ramgoolam's Alliance du Changement won all 60 directly elected seats in November 2024, ending Pravind Jugnauth's government after a wiretapping scandal. Ramgoolam, prime minister for a third time, revisited the terms of the Chagos deal before it was signed in 2025.
power: A parliamentary republic. The prime minister leads the majority in the National Assembly, elected in multi-member constituencies with extra seats to balance communities; the president is chosen by parliament and largely ceremonial.

leaders.gov: Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam, since November 2024
